title: Article 85 — Sessions of Parliament, prorogation and dissolution

content.overview: Article 85 requires the President to summon each House of Parliament from time to time so that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. The President may from time to time prorogue the Houses or either House, and dissolve the House of the People.
content.glance: President summons Houses (max 6-month gap between sessions); may prorogue either/both Houses; may dissolve Lok Sabha only.
content.study:
Article 85:

(1) The President shall from time to time summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, but six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.

(2) The President may from time to time—
(a) prorogue the Houses or either House;
(b) dissolve the House of the People.

Key distinctions:
- Summon: call a session.
- Prorogue: end a session (pending business may be affected as per rules/practice).
- Dissolve: end the life of the Lok Sabha (only the House of the People can be dissolved; Rajya Sabha cannot).

Six-month rule: constitutional maximum gap between sessions of each House.

Examination: state the six-month rule; distinguish summon / prorogue / dissolve; only Lok Sabha is dissolved.

sections.heading: Powers under Article 85
sections.body:
1. Summon each House (six-month maximum gap).
2. Prorogue the Houses or either House.
3. Dissolve the House of the People (not the Council of States).

misconceptions.trap: The President can dissolve the Rajya Sabha.
misconceptions.correction: Only the House of the People can be dissolved. The Council of States is not subject to dissolution (Article 83).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Article 85.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 85 requires the President to summon each House of Parliament from time to time so that not more than six months intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next. The President may prorogue the Houses or either House, and may dissolve the House of the People. The Council of States cannot be dissolved.

examTips: 6-month session gap; summon vs prorogue vs dissolve; only LS dissolved.

keyTakeaways: Art 85: summon (6-month rule), prorogue, dissolve LS only.
